key_insight: Among the HVOF-sprayed cermet coatings tested on 65G steel, WC–Co–Cr delivered the best overall balance of density, hardness, and tribological performance.
engineering_relevance: The results show that binder and carbide composition strongly control coating integrity and wear resistance, guiding material selection for abrasive-adhesive service in machinery, power, and metallurgy.
method: HVOF deposition of WC–Co–Cr, WC–NiCr, WC–Ni, Cr3C2–NiCr, and Al2O3–NiCr coatings on 65G steel
Microstructure and composition assessed by SEM/EDS
Performance evaluated using microhardness, roughness, friction, and adhesion/scratch response
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative testing across multiple coatings, with WC–Co–Cr reaching 1316.87 HV and μ = 0.143, while Al2O3–NiCr showed the poorest combination of hardness and friction.
watch_item: Reported performance depends on spraying conditions and substrate/coating system, so transfer to other HVOF setups or service environments should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: THE EFFECT OF THE COMPOSITION OF METAL-CERAMIC POWDERS ON THE STRUCTURE AND PERFORMANCE PROPERTIES OF COATINGS OBTAINED BY THE HVOF METHOD
